text:
Mia: heads-up: several new users reported 'AuthError: token refresh failed' when trying the next-samplechain starter (LangChain + LlamaIndex). happening during first chat message on deployed preview.
Raj: that's bad. error stack?
Mia: gist with logs: https://gist.github.com/mia/preview-auth-fail. key part:
Mia: ```
Error: AuthError: token refresh failed
  at RedwoodAuth.refresh (node_modules/@redwood/sdk/index.js:412:22)
  at sendRequest (node_modules/@redwood/sdk/index.js:128:15)
```
Priya: I bet it's the way the starter exposes the API key. the sample uses NEXT_PUBLIC_RW_API in client code, which is visible to browsers and also causes server-side code to try refresh with an ephemeral client that lacks private creds.
Noah: yup coincidence: starter index.js has `const rw = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RW_API });` Should be server-only call using RW_SERVER_API_KEY.
Mia: repro steps I used: deploy to Vercel preview, click "Start chat", first message sometimes 401, sometimes passes if you open and close quickly. flakey.
Priya: besides env var fix, we should also make SDK tolerant: if refresh fails, surface clearer error and avoid retry loops that produce duplicate messages in the UI.
Raj: agreed. we should add a guard in the sample: client instantiation in /pages/api/chat.js -> only create server client when running in server context. example snippet: 
Raj: ```js
// pages/api/chat.js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk';
const serverClient = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_SERVER_API_KEY });
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const r = await serverClient.chat.create(...);
  res.json(r);
}
```
Noah: small UX note: the LangChain wrapper in the sample was re-streaming partial tokens after the 401 attempt, causing ghost replies. we should set streaming: true on the adapter and let client-side merge the stream state.
DevEx Bot: CI failed on sample-kit/eval-harness (flaky) in run #112, reran 2x.
Mia: about the eval harness: test_samples/e2e_chat.py is brittle because it assumes deterministic sampling. needs to switch to a semantic checker instead of exact string match. also the harness does a full deploy for each run which is slow and increases flakiness.
Priya: proposal: 1) change env var names in README + starter to server-only use, 2) add guard in starter API route, 3) update LangChain adapter to streaming-safe mode, 4) update eval harness to semantic asserts and reduce deploys by reusing a staging preview.
Raj: I'll open a single PR that touches sample code + README + a small SDK error message tweak. PR #4890. includes tests that mock token refresh failure.
Noah: I'll take the eval harness refactor (reduce deploys + semantic checks). assigning to @Noah. ETA: 3 days.
Mia: filing follow-up issue to audit other starters for NEXT_PUBLIC leakage. https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/6799
Priya: FYI I ran a quick grep across repo and found two other samples referencing NEXT_PUBLIC_RW_API in client code. will list in the issue.
Mia: nice catch. once PR lands, please ping #devex for a quick smoke validation in staging.
Noah: will do. I'll also add a flakiness note to the eval-harness README.
Raj: thanks team. small but high impact onboarding win. :rocket:
Mia: awesome. closing loop here after smoke test passes.
